summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint in messages-send
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js at line 425/436 assembles an outbound HTTPS destination from a String.fromCharCode(...) decimal array. The decoded host is https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The destination is not present in source as a plain string; it is reconstructed at runtime specifically to hide the host from static inspection. Placement inside a Baileys fork's message-send path means the obfuscated endpoint is reached on normal WhatsApp send operations, causing caller-supplied message data and/or session material handled by that code path to be delivered to an author-controlled host rather than only to WhatsApp's infrastructure. Char-code reconstruction of a network host in a messaging library's send routine matches the covert-exfiltration fingerprint for WhatsApp/Baileys forks.
